Phases: 2 · commits d0bdfc8..48ff607 · review: APPROVED

Phase 1 stalled on a bad must_have pattern in the order, not on the code.

The validation module and its unit tests are written and green (`npm test` and `npm run lint` both pass), uncommitted on disk: `src/http/validation.ts`, `test/validation.test.ts`.

I confirmed the diagnosis directly. The order's frontmatter carries `pattern: "lines\\[0\\]\\.quantity"`, and `.claude/lib/yaml-lite.mjs` only strips the quotes, so the doubled backslashes reach `new RegExp` unprocessed. The check therefore looks for the literal text `lines\[0\]\.quantity` (with backslashes) in the test file, which correct test code will never contain. `harness verify` prints `FAIL grep:test/validation.test.ts:lines\\[0\\]\\.quantity` while everything else passes. The artifact is the architect's to edit, so I have not touched it.

Options:

`[c]` continue: architect corrects that one pattern to `lines\[0\]\.quantity`, then the same developer re-verifies and commits phase 1 (recommended, no code change needed)
`[d]` redesign: send the whole order back to the architect
`[x]` abandon the work item

▶ 20260911-invoices-csv-export-endpoint · phase 2/2 blocked · PHASE STALLED on phase 2

The code is done, tested and committed (`ac670ee`): the route, its tests, and a live-server drive all pass. The stall is an artifact defect, not a code one. Two `greps` patterns in the order's own frontmatter (lines 40 and 44 of `work/20260911-invoices-csv-export-endpoint/order.md`) are written as `"invoices\\.csv"`. The harness YAML reader does not unescape, so the regex it builds is `/invoices\\.csv/m`, which demands a literal backslash in the source and can never match. The third pattern on the same file, `text/csv; charset=utf-8`, has no backslash and passes.

Fix is one character on each of two lines in the order (`pattern: invoices\.csv`), which the architect owns; no code changes.
